claim: The 2026 regular season through Week 10 is a 136-game corpus.
live_value: 148 FINAL games (296 club-games). Week 11 has begun.
repo_value: 33 verified rows in board/data/games_2026.csv; 137 cited in board/data/questions.csv
method: Counted FINAL results on each official weekly schedule page for weeks 1-10 and cross-checked the total against the standings page (LV-07). Then re-derived the snapshot-time figure from the same corpus by filtering on game date.
note: The number was right when it was written and is wrong now, which is a different problem from being wrong. 136 is exactly the count of games dated before 2026-11-12, i.e. week 10 had not started; 137 adds the Thursday game. Today 148 games are FINAL. A figure that is correct at capture time but carried as a constant becomes a false statement the moment the season advances - so the corpus figure must be derived from data/week_results_2026.csv at render time, never typed into prose. The real defect is not the number, it is that board/data/games_2026.csv still holds 33 rows against a 148-game corpus, so no ROI can be computed anywhere in that track.

claim: A 148-row results corpus transcribed from the weekly schedule pages reconciles exactly with the official standings.
live_value: 32 clubs, W/L/T, PF and PA all reproduced exactly
method: For every club, summed wins, losses, ties, points-for and points-against from the 148 rows and compared each of the 160 figures against the official standings page. Zero mismatches. Re-runnable: python3 scripts/build_week_results.py --check
note: This is the strongest check available without a second independent source: two different official pages, 148 rows, 160 aggregate figures, no tolerance. A single transposed score would fail it. League totals also balance (sum PF = sum PA).

claim: The committed Week 10 model lines were published before the games were played.
live_value: 11 of 14 kickoffs were still in the future at commit time
method: Matched each of the 14 originated lines to its official final score and read the model file's own 'kickoff' field.
note: 12 of the 14 games now have final scores; 1 game (PIT at CIN) is still in progress and 1 (LAC at BAL) is still to be played. Of the 12 settled games, WAS at NYG was already FINAL when the model file was committed, so it is lookahead-contaminated and is excluded from scoring. That leaves an honest out-of-sample n of 11. See data/line_eval.json.

claim: An official NFL source publishes a depth-chart ordinal that could rank a player as 2nd/3rd/4th string.
source_gap: NFL.com publishes rosters and injury reports but no depth-chart ordinal; club depth pages are club-published, not league-published, and several clubs publish an image rather than a table. There is no official league URL that settles a 32-club depth ranking. This row therefore cannot be marked confirmed and must not be presented as if it had been.
method: Searched the league site for a depth-chart route; none is registered in any session's source list.
note: The repo's existing position (F05) is correct and should stand: backup depth is a model estimate built on third-party chart data, never a league fact, and every use of it is labelled as such.

claim: An official, licensed market price for spreads, totals or props is available to this repo.
source_gap: No NFL-operated page publishes a betting price. Sportsbook pages are operator-published, not league-official, and are geo-gated or non-machine-readable from this environment. There is no official URL for this row.
method: Confirmed across sessions (F07, FLG-010, Q-01) and re-confirmed here: nothing on nfl.com publishes a spread, total, moneyline or prop price.
note: Consequence, stated plainly: closing-line value and ROI cannot be computed for any strategy in this repo, and no leaderboard can rank a staking result. The honest scoreboard is proper-score skill, which needs only results - and those are now verified (LV-07).

claim: Snap counts and official inactive lists are captured, so a backup replacing a starter can be confirmed rather than suspected.
source_gap: The league injury report publishes practice and game designations but not snap counts and not the 90-minute inactive list. No official machine-readable snap-count feed is registered.
method: Checked the official report's columns: Player, Position, Injuries, Practice Status, Game Status. No snap or inactive column exists.
note: The brief's requirement stands unmet and must stay flagged. A replacement can currently be identified from a club depth chart, but 'the backup actually played the starter's snaps' cannot be evidenced from an official league page.

claim: The Week 10 injury report can be reconstructed as a daily series (Wed/Thu/Fri practice progression).
source_gap: The official League injury page renders one current report per week, overwriting the previous day's designations. There is no dated archive URL for the Wednesday or Thursday version of the Week 10 report.
method: Read the live page: it shows one Practice Status and one Game Status per player, with no date axis.
note: This is why the 'DNP -> LP -> FP' trend requirement cannot be satisfied retroactively for Week 10. It has to be captured prospectively, on a schedule, from here on. See the snapshot protocol on the site's method page.

claim: A club depth chart is a durable statement of who will start.
source_gap: Club depth pages carry no league-issued version or effective date, so there is no official reference point against which to prove a chart is current. A chart cannot be shown to be stale from an official source alone.
method: Used the league roster and injury pages as the authority for availability; treated charts as depth-order only, per the existing authority rule.
note: The existing rule - league report owns availability, club chart owns order, every disagreement is published - remains the only defensible position. Any claim that a chart is 'stale' is an inference and is labelled one.
